section.title: Supported scenarios on &skvm;
section.para: &suse; and &sap; maintain a joint support commitment for your traditional virtualized &sap; deployments. This support framework enables you to host production workloads on &skvm; with full confidence, provided your environment conforms to the specific software versions, processor architectures and sizing principles documented by both vendors.

section.title: &sap; application servers and non-HANA databases
section.para: &sap; fully supports traditional &sap; application components, such as ABAP and Java Application Servers (for example, &netweaver;, &s4h; application layers) for your production deployment on &skvm;. This production support is applicable for &sles; 11 SP1 or later as the hypervisor. However, &suse; requires &sles4sapa; as the hypervisor for &sap; workloads.

For relational database management systems (RDBMS) hosting your &sap; database instances, production support on &skvm; covers most enterprise-grade relational databases. This includes &sapase; (&sapasea;) and &ibmdb2;. However, you must respect specific vendor limitations. For example, &sap; explicitly does not support Oracle databases for production use on the &skvm; platform.

Before deployment, you must consult the general support parameters laid out in the official &sapnote;s. For general virtualization support rules, see &sapnote; 1492000. For details regarding the &skvm; support statements and virtualization agreements, see &sapnote; 1522993. This &sapnote; also includes instructions on how to set up host monitoring from within the virtual machines, which is a requirement for running virtualized &sap; applications.

section.title: &hana;
section.para: Due to the high-performance memory-bound nature of &hana;, &sap; supports &kvm; virtualization under strict validation boundaries. You must ensure your sizing, hypervisor setup and configuration adhere to validated hardware topologies to maintain support eligibility. Validated configurations support multiple physical layouts, including single-virtual machine (Single-VM) setups, multi-virtual machine (Multi-VM) configurations, &ha; (HA) cluster nodes and live migration configurations.

To assist you in matching your physical processor configurations with validated software versions, &suse; and &sap; publish specific validation notes. These notes map particular &sles4sapa; service packs and &intel; Xeon processor architectures to your validated workloads. The following table summarizes these validated scenarios:

row.entry: &intel; Xeon E3, E5 and E7 v3 series (Haswell)
4th and 5th Generation &intel; Xeon Scalable Processors (Sapphire Rapids and Emerald Rapids)
2nd, 4th, 5th and 6th Generation &intel; Xeon Scalable Processors (Cascade Lake, Sapphire Rapids, Emerald Rapids* and Granite Rapids*)

para.emphasis: * &sap; validation on-going, check the respective &sapnote; for support status.

section.para: For detailed architecture sizing and configuration guidelines, refer to the official &suse; Best Practices Guides for &hana; on &kvm;, available via the &suse; Documentation site. The respective guides are linked in the previous table. &sapnote; 3430656 provides a list of all &skvm; hypervisors validated for &hana; workloads. For all hypervisors supported to virtualize &hana;, see &sapnote; 1788665.
The guest operating system can be any that is supported both by &suse; as a guest operating system for the specific hypervisor, and by &sap; as an operating system for &hana;.

Through the introduction of Tailored Datacenter Integration (TDI) Phase 5, &sap; began shifting away from established core-to-RAM ratios for &hana; appliances toward workload-based sizing. &sap; also supports workload-based sizing for your &hana; instances virtualized on &skvm;. See &sapnote; 2779240 for details.
